result:
Solution 1 is correct. The count follows from a direct decomposition of the path.

The x- and y-coordinates only ever increase, so the projection of the path onto the xy-plane is a monotone lattice path from (0,0) to (3,3). There are C(6,3) = 20 such projections, passing through 7 vertices v₀, …, v₆.

Kelvin can only change z while sitting at one of these vertices. Points above different xy-vertices are different points, so revisits can only happen within a single vertex. There, the z-moves must all go in one direction (all up or all down), because reversing direction would return to a point already visited.

At each vertex vᵢ, Kelvin therefore enters at some height aᵢ and leaves at some height aᵢ₊₁, moving monotonically between them. Every such pair (aᵢ, aᵢ₊₁) with both in {0,1,2,3} gives a valid, non-repeating, in-bounds walk at that vertex.

The heights are fixed at a₀ = 0 (start) and a₇ = 3 (end). The six intermediate heights a₁, …, a₆ can each be any of 4 values independently, giving 4⁶ = 4096 choices for each xy-path.

Total: 20 × 4096 = 81920.

Solution 2 wrongly rules out detours such as 0→3→0→3 across several vertices, which are valid. Solution 3 also undercounts and ends with an unjustified guess.

CHOICE: 1
